#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Destination is not decided in this repo. Set it via the BACKUP_DEST
# environment variable when scheduling the job (e.g. in the crontab/systemd
# unit created by register-job.sh), either as:
#   - a local/mounted path, e.g. BACKUP_DEST=/mnt/backups
#   - a remote scp-style destination, e.g. BACKUP_DEST=user@host:/path/to/backups
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup.sh: BACKUP_DEST is not set; refusing to run without a backup destination" >&2
    echo "backup.sh: set BACKUP_DEST to a local path or user@host:/path before running" >&2
    exit 1
fi

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Looks like a remote destination (user@host:/path) -> use scp.
        scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # Local path or mount point -> plain copy. Create it if missing.
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"/
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
chmod +x backup.sh; sh -n backup.sh && echo "syntax ok"
mkdir -p logs && echo test > logs/test.log
BACKUP_DEST=/tmp/backup-dest ./backup.sh
ls -la /tmp/backup-dest
rm -f logs-*.tar.gz
rm -rf /tmp/backup-dest logs
unset BACKUP_DEST
./backup.sh; echo "exit code: $?"
